Generated from the module documentation of [`crates/canon/src/ir/mod.rs`](https://github.com/beyond10x/canon/blob/main/crates/canon/src/ir/mod.rs).

`canon-ir/1`, the normalized form evaluators consume (design § 30).

`compile` is a pure function of a `protocol/1` document: it validates the document and, when it
is valid, returns its `Ir`. The IR differs from the source in exactly these ways:

- **Canonical ordering.** Declarations are keyed and ordered by identifier, not by the order they
  are written in. The members of an `all` or `any` predicate are sorted by `canonical_order`,
  and an action's capability requirements (by capability, then by scope, one without a scope
  first, a scope comparing its keys and values in key order), the evidence kinds it may
  produce and the artifacts it revises, the claims an
  invalidation rule invalidates, the values a case input declares, the values an input test
  lists and the dimensions an evidence match demands independence on by identifier, and the
  outcomes a `children` form lists by code point.
- **No repetition.** Each of those ten lists holds every member once: in three-valued logic
  `all` and `any` are idempotent, and the three action lists, the invalidated claims, the two
  lists of input values, the dimensions of `independent_on` and the outcomes of `children` are
  sets. A kind an action lists twice may produce once, and is judgement-decided when either
  listing is.
- **Explicit defaults.** Every field is present. An absent description or effect is `null`; an
  evidence match without a result has `"result": null`; a claim test without `is` has
  `"is": "true"`; an action without a precondition has the precondition `{"all": []}`, which is
  true; absent lists and sections are empty. The fifteen exceptions are an evidence kind's
  `max_age` and its `supplied_by`, the `subject` of an evidence match or an order form, an
  evidence match's `independent_on`, an obligation's `applicable_when`, an action's
  `arguments`, an action's `case_open`, an action's `author` and its `revises`, the
  `decided_by` of an evidence kind an action may produce, the `scope` of a capability
  requirement, the `revision` of a `children` form, the `invalidation` section, the `case`
  section and the `independence_dimensions` section: each written only when it is declared (a
  scope only when it names a key, a `children` form's `revision` only when it is `current`, an
  action's `author` only as `"author": "judgement"`, its `revises` only when it lists an
  artifact, a production's `decided_by` only as `"decided_by": "judgement"`, a section only
  when it holds a rule, an input or a dimension), so the IR of a protocol that declares none of
  them is the IR it was before they existed. A production's `decided_by` is resolved: the
  action's `author` when the production declares none (story:judgement-marking), so
  `author: program` and a `decided_by` equal to the action's `author` compile to no key. An evidence kind's `supplied_by` is the protocol id as
  declared, a name nothing resolves (story:supplied-evidence). A capability requirement is `{"capability": …}`, or `{"capability": …, "scope": {<key>: <value>, …}}` with a scope (story:capability-scope). The `independence_dimensions`
  section is `{<id>: {"description": …}}`. The `case` section is
  `{"inputs": {<id>: {"description": …, "values": [...]}}}`. An order form is written as
  authored: `{"first": {"kind": …, "result": …}}`, `{"before": {"first": …, "then": …}}`,
  `{"after": {"first": …, "then": {"kind": …, "result": …}}}` and
  `{"since": {"last": …, "then": {"kind": …, "result": …}}}`.
  The form over the child cases is `{"children": {"in": [...]}}`, or `{"children": {"in": [...], "revision": "current"}}` when it reads only the records about the current revision of
  their subject (story:child-outcome-revision): `revision: any` reads what no key reads and is
  written as no key. An action's `case_open` is `{"protocol": …, "subject": …}`, as declared
  (story:case-composition).
  An action's `arguments` is its JSON Schema as declared, the same JSON value, its object keys
  sorted like every object's (story:action-arguments).
- **No authoring sugar.** A claim test is always `{"claim": {"id": …, "is": …}}`, whichever way
  it was written, and an input test `{"input": {"id": …, "in": [...]}}`. An outcome that
  requires an explicit decision has the requirement `{"decision": <name>}`, as written; any
  other requirement is its predicate.
- **Resolved references.** Only a document the validator accepts compiles, so every claim and
  evidence kind the IR references is declared in it (`case_outcome` wherever a `children` form
  reads it), and so is every artifact an evidence match or an order form names as its subject,
  an action revises (`revises`) or opens a case about (`case_open`) or an invalidation rule
  names as its upstream
  artifact, every input an input test names, with every value it lists, and every dimension an
  evidence match demands independence on.

The IR carries the protocol id and revision (design § 37) and nothing about where the document
came from: no path, no working directory, no time. `Ir::canonical_json` is its one
serialization, and the bytes are suitable for hashing: documents that differ only in the ways
listed above give the same bytes. Other logical equivalences are not normalized, so they give
different bytes: a one-member `all` or `any` and its member, a nested `all` inside an `all` and
the flattened list, `not` of `not` and what it negates, and maximum ages of the same length
written in different units (`60m` and `1h`).

`check_openings` takes a set of compiled protocols and refuses it when their actions'
`case_open` openings form a cycle (`case-open-cycle`, D206): a protocol opens a case under
another when one of its actions names that protocol in `case_open`, and a cycle is a path of
openings back to where it began. The refusal names the first cycle a walk from the least
protocol id on any cycle finds, in the order its openings go, back to that id
(`protocols open cases under each other in a cycle: audit -> review -> audit`). An opening
under a protocol outside the set closes no cycle; a chain of openings is accepted.

A protocol that imports others (`imports:`, story:protocol-imports) compiles only composed with
the documents it imports, directly or through another import: `compose` turns the root and
those documents into one `protocol/1` document without imports, and `compile` compiles that
like any other. Compiled alone, such a protocol is refused, each import `missing-import`. The
composition is a pure function of the documents passed to it, whatever their order, and reads
nothing else. Every imported declaration is inlined under its own identifier, a declaration two
imports share once (identical declarations are those with the same `canon-ir/1` entry, so two
that differ only in the ways listed above are one), and a redeclaration the import lists under
`refines` replaces the imported declaration; the IR names the root's id and revision only and
holds no import, so it is the IR of one document holding the same declarations inline, byte for
byte. Each import pins the revision of the document it reads and its `digest`: `sha256:` and
the SHA-256, in lowercase hexadecimal, of that document's `canon-ir/1` bytes, compiled with its
own imports.

`compose` refuses, in this order, stopping after the first step that finds a problem: a
protocol supplied twice, the root's id included (`duplicate-import-document`); a malformed
`imports` section (an import id or a `refines` entry that is not an identifier, an import id
listed twice, a digest of another form: `invalid-identifier`, `duplicate-identifier`,
`invalid-import-digest`); an import no supplied document is (`missing-import`) and a supplied
document no import names (`unused-import`); an import cycle (`import-cycle`, naming it from
the first protocol on it a walk from the root meets, back to that protocol), before any pin is
read, since no pin of a cycle can be right; then each document, every import before the
documents that import it: a pinned revision (`import-revision-mismatch`) or digest
(`import-digest-mismatch`, printing both digests) the supplied document does not have, a
`refines` entry its import does not declare (`undeclared-refinement`), an identifier two imports
declare with different `canon-ir/1` entries in one section that the document does not redeclare
(`conflicting-imports`), and a redeclaration its import does not list under `refines`
(`unrefined-redeclaration`). A problem of an imported document itself is wrapped in
`invalid-import`, naming it. The composed root is validated like any document, so an imported
action that opens a case under the root's id is `self-opened-case`.
